text: On Richard Lazarus's appraisal theory, what makes anger the specific emotion it is (rather than fear or guilt)?
choices: A distinctive autonomic signature shared by all humans
A high-arousal, negative-valence point in a two-dimensional affect space
The perception of bodily trembling and muscular readiness
Its distinctive 'core relational theme' -- appraising a demeaning offence by another agent whom one can hold responsible
explanation: Lazarus individuates emotions by their core relational themes: anger = a blameworthy wrong done to me, fear = an uncertain threat, guilt = my own moral transgression. Option 0 is basic-emotion theory; option 1 is Barrett's core-affect view; option 2 is the James-Lange feeling account.
